facts.text: The project captures data from a Rigol DS1000Z series oscilloscope over LAN
The oscilloscope class extends the device transport class
The device constructor sends *IDN? on connect
The *IDN? reply is split into manufacturer, device name, serial number and firmware version
The active-channel list starts empty and get_active_channel fills it
get_active_channel builds channel names CHAN1 through CHANn from the configured channel count
A channel is kept as active when its display query answers '1\n'
The clone's example constructs the oscilloscope with four channels over USB
plot reads the timebase scale with :TIM:SCAL? and the timebase offset with :TIM:OFFS?
plot reads each active channel's vertical scale with :<CHANn>:SCAL? and offset with :<CHANn>:OFFS?
The captured time axis runs from time_offset - 6 * time_scale to time_offset + 6 * time_scale
plot sets the waveform point mode with :WAV:POIN:MODE RAW, reads :WAV:DATA? with the channel name and writes :KEY:FORCE
The waveform reply drops its first 10 characters before the samples are converted
plot references tUnit, but tUnit is only named in commented-out code, so the method cannot complete
The serial transport writes a command and reads one line back
The LAN transport sends *OPC? until it reads 1\n, then sends the command with a newline and reads until a newline
The LAN transport is a copy of the Python 2.7 telnetlib with a patch that keeps null characters
The USB transport read ignores its command argument and sends *OPC? without returning a value
